text:
Sam (eng-infra): monitor alert - us-west-2 gpu pool-3 reporting a spike in correctable memory errors. ~120 correctables/min across 7 nodes, started ~2m ago. Not seeing XIDs yet. Do we run auto-drain or put nodes into a probe state?

Monitor Bot: ALERT: Correctable ECC error rate >100/min for pool=us-west-2-pool-3 (group_size=7). Dashboard: https://console.redwood.internal/d/pools/pool-3?panel=ECC :rotating_light:

Liam: do we have per-card breakdown? could be one flaky card on multiple hosts or many cards with small noise.

Anya: quick look — 4 hosts show sustained per-card high rates, 3 hosts just blips. I'd rather soft-drain (no new pods) + run diagnostics than immediate hard drain. Avoids capacity churn.

Sam (eng-infra): current auto-drain is threshold=50/min sustained 30s -> autodrain. That felt aggressive in the past. Propose we tune to add a soft state.

Maria: proposal for playbook:
- SOFT-DRAIN (probing): mark sched=NoNew, tag ecc:probing, run diag job 5m, collect nvml logs.
- If diag shows stable drop -> unmark.
- If errors persist or XID appears -> HARD-DRAIN (cordon+evict) then RMA.
- Add capacity gate: skip soft-drain if spare capacity <10%.

Liam: +1 to soft-drain. Also only hard-drain if corrected errors correlate with XID or NVML count is monotonically increasing for 5m.

Anya: prometheus snippet I'm using to separate bursty vs sustained:
```promql
sum by(card, host)(increase(nvidia_hw_ecc_corrected_total[1m]))
```
Alert when card-level >10/min for 5m OR host-level >60/min for 3m.

Sam (eng-infra): for automation logic I suggest: soft-drain if host-level >40/min sustained 45s -> fire diag job 5m -> hard-drain if >80/min over 2m OR any XID. That gives a repro window.

Ops Bot: Created tasks: RED-4567 update-autodrain-playbook (assignee: Sam), RED-4568 diag-job-runbook (assignee: Maria).

Maria: also add node annotation history: last_7d_ecc_counts to help RMA decisions. QE wants the trend not just the current spike.

Liam: console changes: show 'soft-drain' state count + estimated backlog impact when toggled. Helps SRE during incidents.

Anya: small nit — use a 3-point rolling average on the rate to smooth telemetry before making state transitions. Helps ignore microbursts.

Sam (eng-infra): agree. Owners: Sam -> operator PR for state machine + thresholds, Maria -> diag job + runbook, Anya -> prometheus alerts + dashboard, Liam -> console metric panel. Target: staging deploy by EOD tomorrow, prod after 24h of staging.

Maria: playbook text draft for runbook page:
- detect -> soft-drain (NoNew) -> run diag job (5m) -> analyze (nvml logs, corrected/XID correlation) -> escalate to hard-drain + RMA if persistent or XID seen.
- thresholds: soft 40/m sustained 45s, hard 80/m sustained 2m, XID immediate.
- capacity gate: skip soft when spare <10% or business hours override flag set.
- tagging: ecc:probing on soft-drain, ecc:flaky after 3 soft-drains in 7d.

Liam: +1. Also include a short CLI snippet for manual ops:
```bash
kubectl label node <node> ecc=probing
kubectl cordon <node>
kubectl apply -f diag-job.yaml --namespace infra-diagnostics
```

Sam (eng-infra): I'll open the PR. @Anya please add the alert rules and panels. We'll run it in staging this week.

Anya: on it — will sync tomorrow 9am PT to walk through alert behavior in staging. :white_check_mark:
